note: Adapted from the species-level description in Hill (1942), original in English; the original combination is Glyptotermes brevicornis Froggatt, 1897, with the headline reading Calotermes (Glyptotermes) brevicornis (Froggatt). Measurements in mm; they are transcribed in the three columns of the original, Sydney / southern Queensland / northern Queensland, and the first column has no length with wings. Distribution: Mackay, Queensland (type locality), Mt. Tambourine, Imbil, MacPherson Range, Glasshouse Mountains, Brisbane, Cedar Creek, Malanda, Herberton, Ravenshoe, Lake Barrine, Cairns, Gordonvale, the Bellenden Ker area, Innisfail, Palm Island; Wauchope, Coffs Harbour, Sydney, Grafton and Narrabeen, New South Wales; Lord Howe Island; Norfolk Island; Fiji (doubtful). Synonyms: C. affinis Mjöberg, C. trilineatus Mjöberg, C. dubius Mjöberg, C. nigrolabrum Hill, C. claripennis Hill and C. perangustus Hill are all placed in this species. Type material: the original states that the type series appears to consist of wings only, with nothing available for a neotype, and that paratypes of the synonymous species are in the Natural History Museum.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: A small, variable-sized species; upper surface reddish brown (much darker in dealated reproductives), wing pads darker, sternites and tibiae pale brown, femora paler, wings brown with darker veins. Head (Fig. 38) finely shagreened, with a few short hairs, slightly longer than wide, sides slightly narrowed posteriorly, vertex slightly concave, with a few wrinkles at the middle on the same line as the compound eyes. Compound eyes variable in size. Antennae 13—16-segmented, usually 15. Pronotum about as wide as the head, anterior margin concave, sides rounded, sides and posterior margin with distinct impressions. Costa and subcosta of the wings very short, cubitus indistinct except at the base, running slightly above the middle of the wing, with 8—12 branches. Wing membrane with numerous micrasters. Legs short and stout, tibial spurs long, finely serrate or without serrations. Measurements (mm; the original gives three columns, Sydney / southern Queensland / northern Queensland): length with wings — / 10.00—11.50 / 10.50—12.00; length without wings 5.30—5.80 / 5.50—6.50 / 5.75—7.50; head length (to apex of labrum) 1.08—1.21 / 1.32—1.50 / 1.39—1.68; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.84—0.94 / 0.91—1.21 / 1.17—1.28; head width 0.97—1.10 / 1.13—1.28 / 1.21—1.46; pronotum length 0.58 / 0.58—0.66 / 0.69—0.80; pronotum width 0.91—0.95 / 1.06—1.24 / 1.17—1.43.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Size very variable, small to medium-sized, individuals in young colonies relatively very small. Head ochraceous yellowish brown, gradually becoming yellowish brown (russet) anteriorly, mandibles black, dark chestnut at the base. Head (Fig. 39) long and narrow, sides parallel, finely shagreened, anterodorsal margin with rather indistinct lateral projections. Postclypeus short and wide, with a row of about 8 hairs near the anterior margin. Frons with a broad, shallow depression, slightly wrinkled. Labrum short and wide, margins with a narrow impression. Mandibles short, width and dentition very variable: basal half of the right mandible with 2 short teeth, middle third of the left mandible with 3 smaller teeth; in one case the right upper mandible had only 1 very short tooth and the left 3 degenerate teeth. Antennae 11—15-segmented, usually 13. Pronotum about as wide as the head, margins with a narrow impression, anterior margin deeply and broadly concave. Legs very short and stout, hind femur more than half as wide as long. Tibial spurs large, faintly serrate. Measurements (mm; the original gives three columns, Sydney / southern Queensland / northern Queensland): body length 7.25 / 4.50—7.35 / 6.25—9.75; head length including mandibles 2.93 / 2.09—3.11 / 2.86—4.66; head length (to clypeal suture) 2.27 / 1.50—2.38 / 2.12—3.22; head width 1.32 / 1.06—1.35 / 1.28—1.87; pronotum length 0.66 / 0.40—0.66 / 0.56—0.84; pronotum width 1.17 / 0.93—1.32 / 1.21—1.68.
